newsitem.title: USA: Citadel students get sensitivity training.
newsitem.headline: Citadel students get sensitivity training.

text.p: Regular classes were cancelled at the Citadel Tuesday while the state-funded military college conducted sensitivity training for its 1,800 cadets, Citadel officials said.

The college had said it would bring in experts to lead discussions and lecture on diversity issues, among them Evelyn Foote, a one-star general on the task force investigating allegations of sexual harassment in the U.S. Army.

The Citadel waged a lengthy legal fight against co-education before enrolling the first four women members in its corps of cadets last summer. Two of the four later left the school, charging physical abuse and sexual harassment that led to punishment of 14 male cadets, including the dismissal of one and the resignation of three others.
School officials have quietly conducted sensitivity training since then and have brought in consultants to evaluate conditions for women students.
The number of women in the Citadel's corps of cadets seemed likely to increase with the class entering in August as school officials said more than three dozen had been accepted.
